newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium sinks but sagging dlr boosts trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium sinks but sagging dlr boosts trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed near their daily limit-lows on Monday, due to the dollar's weakness against the yen, traders said.
But they said large fluctuations in the currency market breathed life back into trade in aluminium futures, which have seen daily turnover dwindle since the contract was launched in April.
"We've seen strong fresh buying interest (from individual investors)," said a trader with a major trading house.
Traders said TOCOM prices were high compared to London aluminium prices under current foreign exchange rates.
TOCOM yen-based aluminium futures ranged from 4.8 yen to 5.9 yen per kg lower compared to their Friday close.
Benchmark April 1998 gave up 5.3 yen to close at 200.5 yen per kg, renewing its previous contract low of 205.8 yen on Friday. It had hit an intra-day low of 199.8 yen.
All contracts plunged their six yen daily price limit at the opening.
Trade volume jumped to 8,736 lots, the third largest after 19,645 lots on April 7, when Tokyo aluminium futures were launched, and 8,897 lots on April 10.
Traders said prices were likely to advance in the near term, helped by the metal's fundamental strength, evident in steady declines in London warehouse stocks.
